title: VPC monitoring module: upgrade hooks, canary health-checks, and packaging for Prom/Graf/OTel/log-shipping
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Implement a Terraform module for Private/VPC deployments that bundles Prometheus (operator-based), Grafana, OpenTelemetry Collector, and a lightweight log-shipping agent. The module must include safe upgrade hooks, automated canary health checks that run as part of Terraform apply/upgrade, and opinionated defaults for storage/retention and networking to work inside customer VPCs. This ticket covers the first cut of the module, documentation, CI tests, and a staged rollout plan to Dedicated and Private customers.

Goals:
- Provide a single IaC module customers can install to get a fully supported telemetry stack in their VPC/private cluster.
- Make upgrades low-risk via preflight checks, canary upgrades, and automated health probes.
- Ensure the module is configurable (namespaces, storage sizes, remote_write endpoints, otel pipelines, log targets) but has secure safe defaults.

Constraints and trade-offs considered:
- Using Helm provider vs Kubernetes manifests: Helm gives us better lifecycle/upgrades and reuse of upstream charts (prom-operator, grafana, otel-collector). We will standardize on Helm releases managed by Terraform Helm provider so operators can reason about chart versions.
- Stateful upgrades (Prometheus) present the highest risk. We will avoid disruptive defaults (small retention, PVC expansion during migration) and provide an optional snapshot/backup hook for major upgrades.
- We want zero-downtime for most minor patch upgrades; where that's not feasible, the canary flow will detect regressions and mark the upgrade failed for manual rollback.

Module outputs and behavior (high level):
- Installs HelmRelease resources for prometheus-operator (kube-prometheus-stack), grafana, and otel-collector using the Terraform Helm provider.
- Installs a small log forwarder (vector or fluentd) as a DaemonSet to ship logs to the configured target.
- Creates ServiceMonitors/PodMonitors and PrometheusRules per customer config.
- Adds a pre-upgrade hook (null_resource local-exec or external provisioner) that runs: terraform plan validations, a kubectl readiness check for critical resources, and optional PV snapshots.
- Runs a post-upgrade canary job: deploys a tiny test workload that emits known metrics and logs, then verifies ingestion via the collector and that Grafana dashboards show the metric within a time window. Failure aborts the automation and flags the release for manual review.

Security considerations:
- All chart values default to RBAC-limited service accounts; TLS is enabled for Grafana and endpoints where supported.
- Logs and metrics remote_write endpoints are declared as inputs (no hardcoded secrets); module supports KMS-backed secret injection via external provider.

Deliverables:
- Terraform module in terraform/modules/vpc-observability with docs.
- CI pipeline that runs terraform fmt/validate/checkov and an integration job applying the module into an ephemeral cluster for smoke tests.
- Runbook describing upgrade steps, rollback, and common failures.
acceptance_criteria: Terraform module lives under terraform/modules/vpc-observability and is importable by customers
Module exposes inputs for namespace, storage_class, prometheus_retention, grafana_admin_password_secret, otel_config, log_forwarder_target
Upgrade path includes preflight checks and optional PV snapshot step for stateful workloads
Post-upgrade canary smoke test runs automatically and fails the apply if ingestion or health checks fail
CI runs integration smoke tests in ephemeral cluster and passes on PRs
Documentation and runbook added to Confluence with example var files and rollback steps
